reports.title: Fusion and materialization boundaries in GPU analytical query pipelines
reports.scope_and_novelty_assessment: The report answers the assigned finite question, remains within its named mechanism boundary, and is distinct from indexed/reviewed adjacent reports. No new implementation or product recommendation is made.
reports.source_accuracy: Verified against the linked original papers or official API/vendor documentation; claims remain bounded by the source environment and timing contract.

source_checks.source: Wu et al., Optimizing Data Warehousing Applications for GPUs Using Kernel Fusion/Fission (2012)
source_checks.verified: The controlled pair of random-int32 SELECTs keeps 25%; reported average fused throughput is 49.9% above host round-trip and 6.2% above retaining the intermediate in GPU memory. The paper separates those throughput findings from GPU-only compute and identifies the round-trip as 54.0% of total time for that arm.
source_checks.scope_limit: Fermi/C2070-era measurements and manually transformed kernels; not a portable threshold.

source_checks.source: Cao et al., GPU Database Systems Characterization and Optimization (PVLDB 17(3), 2023)
source_checks.verified: Q21 Table 4 gives TQP idx_select 9.55 ms/23.13%; the paper describes idx_select as creating a tensor after predicate evaluation. It reports 172 BlazingSQL and 190 TQP kernels versus four each for Crystal and HeavyDB, with the hash-join build separated.
source_checks.scope_limit: Cross-system characterization, not a controlled fusion-only ablation; the report says so.

source_checks.source: Wu et al., Red Fox: An Execution Environment for Relational Query Processing on GPUs (CGO 2014)
source_checks.verified: Section 5.3 supports the Q1 plan-ordering example: selection moved earlier, aggregation performed as soon as ready, intermediate footprint halved, and 0.16 s execution excluding PCIe, reported as 1.8x faster than original.
source_checks.scope_limit: Plan reordering, not a fusion ablation.

source_checks.source: Menon et al., Relaxed Operator Fusion for In-Memory Databases (PVLDB 11(1), 2017)
source_checks.verified: The staged fusion/compiler analogy is CPU/in-memory and the report explicitly denies transfer of its performance numbers to GPU.

nonblocking_review_notes: The report correctly labels its byte/launch model as analytical and distinguishes controlled Fermi microbenchmarks from cross-system Q21 characterization.

preserve_caveats: C2070 measurements and Red Fox plan-reordering are historical, system-specific evidence, not a controlled universal fusion crossover.
Cao et al. compare different query systems rather than isolating fusion as a single experimental variable.
The byte/launch model is arithmetic, not measured bandwidth or a Strata/Arc result.

reports.title: Tile-local attachment lifetime and external-memory traffic in tile-based rendering
reports.scope_and_novelty_assessment: The report answers the assigned finite question, remains within its named mechanism boundary, and is distinct from indexed/reviewed adjacent reports. No new implementation or product recommendation is made.
reports.source_accuracy: Verified against the linked original papers or official API/vendor documentation; claims remain bounded by the source environment and timing contract.

source_checks.verified: The retrieved official build metadata reports version 1.4.365 dated 2026-10-02. The normative STORE_OP_NONE definition says no store access only when the pass writes no values; if it writes values it behaves like DONT_CARE. The report distinguishes that from mutable guide advice.
source_checks.scope_limit: The URL tracks latest; report pins the observed version/date.

source_checks.verified: Guide describes tile size as opaque, says subpass merge is implementation-dependent, points to merge feedback, and documents transient/lazy attachments and inline MSAA resolve as opportunities rather than universal physical guarantees.
source_checks.scope_limit: Mutable guide, explicitly labeled non-normative and retrieval-dated in report.

source_checks.verified: The API enables drivers to minimize load/store traffic, but runtime mapping to ordinary surfaces and lack of performance benefit on unsupported drivers are documented; application dependency/resource-state duties remain.

The cited 1440p RGBA8 60-FPS 4x-MSAA round-trip and inline-resolve arithmetic is present in the 2021 guide. The report labels its separate 1920x1080 arithmetic as a byte model, not measured bandwidth.

source_checks.source: Arm GPU Best Practices Developer Guide, issue 10
source_checks.verified: AFBC is described as transparent where eligible; issue 10 documents that transient-attachment usage can block AFBC before Valhall, and warns that image/storage/access choices can prevent compression or trigger decompression.

source_checks.source: Apple, Tailor Your Apps for Apple GPUs and Tile-Based Deferred Rendering
source_checks.verified: Apple documentation describes imageblock/tile memory shared between fragment and tile stages, and combining rendering and compute in a pass through tile shaders.

nonblocking_review_notes: The 1,872 whitespace-token count includes source ledger and structure; the body through the source ledger is 1,573 words and fits the substantive 1,300–1,700 budget.
The STORE_OP_NONE guide/spec distinction is handled correctly; mutable guide and vendor examples remain explicitly version/device bounded.

keys: API content/lifetime contract vs physical DRAM behavior
store/load and MSAA resolve byte arithmetic
AFBC access constraints and portability limits
preserve_caveats: The mutable Vulkan guide and Apple page are retrieval-dated; the normative Vulkan specification is identified as 1.4.365 dated 2026-10-02.
Subpass merge, tile residency, and compression are implementation/device choices; no Intel compute or Arc claim follows.
Arm AFBC restrictions and Apple imageblock behavior apply only to documented vendor generations/APIs.

reports.title: Direction-optimized single-GPU BFS frontier representation and switching costs
reports.scope_and_novelty_assessment: The report answers the assigned finite question, remains within its named mechanism boundary, and is distinct from indexed/reviewed adjacent reports. No new implementation or product recommendation is made.
reports.source_accuracy: Verified against the linked original papers or official API/vendor documentation; claims remain bounded by the source environment and timing contract.

source_checks.source: Beamer et al., Direction-Optimizing Breadth-First Search (SC 2012)
source_checks.verified: The paper documents push/pull, queue-to-bitmap conversion, that a directed graph may require an inverse graph that nearly doubles storage, and the CPU-tuned alpha=14/beta=24 thresholds. It also records conversion and frontier-degree accounting overhead and long-tail counterexamples.
source_checks.scope_limit: Shared-memory CPU evidence, not a GPU threshold.

source_checks.source: Wang et al., Gunrock: A High-Performance Graph Processing Library on the GPU (PPoPP 2016)
source_checks.verified: The original paper gives the frontier-bitmap pull implementation and 1.52x scale-free and 1.28x small-degree/large-diameter BFS group speedups; the report identifies K40c/dataset/timing context and limits interpretation to that system.
source_checks.scope_limit: Historical K40c group-level result, not a universal graph-family rule.

source_checks.verified: Table 9 and §4.3.1 give |Ef*|>|E|/10 for push-to-pull and the reverse below the same estimate, with d|Vf|≈|Ef| and |Eu|≈|E| approximations; §4.3 reports both CSR/CSC plus a single-format memory/performance tradeoff and sparse/dense vectors.
source_checks.scope_limit: Pinned arXiv v1; report preserves the paper’s approximate cost model.

source_checks.verified: The source reports the Titan Xp experiments: top-down best on 21/38 regular and 7/23 irregular graphs; bottom-up on 15/38 regular and 5/23 irregular; hybrid on 6/23 irregular. For the eight larger graphs, first three regular favor bottom-up and five irregular favor hybrid. The report preserves graph-set and format/setup caveats.
source_checks.scope_limit: Paper’s named graph sets and timing boundaries; incomparable to Beamer/Gunrock/GraphBLAST absolute rates.

nonblocking_review_notes: The analytic expected-prefix model is not presented as measured TEPS; CPU, K40c, Titan Xp, and GraphBLAST historical observations remain separated.
The TurboBFS prose distinguishes graph-family counts and marks preprocessing/timing ambiguities rather than normalizing headline rates.

keys: pull prefix scans and early exit
preserve_caveats: Beamer alpha/beta thresholds come from a shared-memory CPU study and are not GPU prescriptions.
Gunrock and TurboBFS results are historical named-device measurements with distinct datasets and metrics.
TurboBFS graph conversion/setup timing boundaries and undirected stored-arc conventions remain unclear; absolute TEPS should not be compared across papers.
No Intel Arc/SYCL prediction or Strata adoption follows.
